deep.reconstruction:
Authorship and context. This page is not a Riemann research note. It is part of a letter or referee report written after Riemann's death about the posthumous edition of Riemann's memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung'. The page references (pp. 289–303) and the equation numbers (Gl. 8, 13, 15, 16) refer to that edition.
- 'Herr H.' is almost certainly K. Hattendorff, who edited the memoir (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867).
- The writer appeals to 'Herr Prof. Weierstraß', who possesses still more complete formulas. He also says he has his own 'sorgfältige Ausarbeitung' on the same question. This points strongly to H. A. Schwarz, who worked on minimal surfaces in the Weierstrass school.
- The recipient is probably one of the editors of Riemann's Werke (Dedekind or Weber).
- The phrase 'in der Riemannschen Abhandlung' confirms that the author is not Riemann.

Point 1 (critique of p. 303: difference of two infinite areas). The edition compares the areas of two surface pieces (sectors) that extend to infinity and speaks of their difference. The writer objects that a 'difference of two infinite quantities' is meaningful only as lim (F1(R) − F2(R)) for a specified exhaustion with finite limit.
- In modern terms: the area difference must be defined by a regularization.
- Example he gives: cut both infinite sectors by the same plane, take the difference of the finite areas, then let the plane recede.
- Without such a specification the passage is meaningless and should be deleted. This is all the more so because Riemann's memoir never treats the global area minimum ('Minimum des Flächeninhalts im Ganzen').

Point 2 (critique of the constant count, note on pp. 301–302). The edition claims that the number of constants of the problem equals the number of constants of the solution. The solution is expressed through an auxiliary variable t, with 2A+B+C+E constants a, a', b, c, e (singular or branch points and related parameters).
- The writer notes that t is only an auxiliary uniformizing variable.
- It may be replaced by any fractional linear (Möbius) function of itself, t -> (p t + q)/(r t + s). The text says 'gebrochene rationale Function ersten Grades'.
- Since the points are presumably real (boundary on the real t-axis), the admissible substitutions form a 3-real-parameter group, PSL(2,R).
- Hence three of the constants can be fixed arbitrarily, e.g. three points sent to 0, 1, ∞.
- So the 2A+B+C+E quantities are equivalent to only 2A+B+C+E−3 essential constants.
- The solution side therefore has too few constants, and Hattendorff's count is inaccurate.
- A struck sentence leaves open whether the multiplicative constant in u should also be counted as essential.

Point 3 (struck passage on missing constants). The writer asks where constants were forgotten. He arrives at the integrals K1 and K2, which must also contain constants. He declines to decide at once whether these are already contained in the constants α, α', … of formula 16.

Continuation on the next page. Here he resolves the question:
- K1 and K2 are two solutions of the second-order linear ODE (15).
- By Abel's identity their Wronskian is K1 K2' − K2 K1' = Const·dv/dt.
- The multiplicative constant drops out of the ratio H = K2/K1.
- One should simply take η = (αK1+βK2)/(γK1+δK2), a quotient of two arbitrary particular solutions.
- This has 4 complex parameters modulo a common factor, i.e. 3 complex = 6 real constants, whereas H. counted only 3.

Closing remarks on this page. He concludes 'es ist gar kein Verlaß auf Herrn H.' and recommends striking Hattendorff's description of his work as a 'sorgfältige' Überarbeitung.
errors: No mathematical error by the writer is visible on this page. The 3-constant reduction is correct provided the points a, a', b, c, e lie on (or are symmetric with respect to) the real t-axis, so that only real Möbius maps are allowed. If complex Möbius maps were allowed, the freedom would be 3 complex = 6 real parameters.
The criticism of the infinite-area difference is mathematically sound: such a difference is exhaustion-dependent unless a regularization is specified.
The struck-through passage about K1 and K2 was explicitly left undecided by the writer. It is resolved on the next page.

results.what: A difference of two infinite areas is meaningful only via a specified common exhaustion (e.g. cutting both sectors by the same plane) with a finite limit.
results.modern_name: Regularized / renormalized area comparison (exhaustion-dependent improper difference)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard analysis; for minimal surfaces, comparison of infinite pieces goes back to the Schwarz / Weierstrass era

results.what: The auxiliary variable t may be changed by a real fractional linear transformation, so three of the parameters a, a', b, c, e are inessential (normalizable). The count becomes 2A+B+C+E−3.
results.modern_name: Normalization by PSL(2,R) (three-point normalization); parameter counting / moduli in Schwarz–Christoffel and Riemann–Hilbert-type problems

results.what: (Next page) The ratio η of two solutions of a second-order linear ODE, taken as general solution pairs, gives η = (αK1+βK2)/(γK1+δK2) with 6 real constants. The Wronskian constant is irrelevant to the ratio.
results.modern_name: Projective (Möbius) ambiguity of the ratio of solutions; Schwarzian derivative / Abel's identity
results.usually_credited_to: Abel (Wronskian identity); Schwarz and Riemann (ratio of solutions and Schwarzian, 1850s–1870s)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is not Riemann's own work. It is a post-1866 editorial critique, most likely by H. A. Schwarz, of Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir. The mathematics (regularizing infinite area differences, Möbius normalization of three parameters, projective ambiguity of solution ratios) is routine for the period. Schwarz's criticism of Hattendorff's edition is of mild historical interest for the editorial history of Riemann's Werke, but nothing here is a new result.

checkable.sympy: t,p,q,r=symbols('t p q r',real=True); m=(t-p)*(q-r)/((t-r)*(q-p)); [simplify(m.subs(t,p)), simplify(m.subs(t,q)), limit(m,t,r)]
checkable.asserts: A real Möbius map sends three arbitrary real points p, q, r to 0, 1, ∞. Hence three real parameters can be normalized away.

checkable.sympy: z1,z2,z3,z4,a,b,c,d=symbols('z1 z2 z3 z4 a b c d'); f=lambda z:(a*z+b)/(c*z+d); cr=lambda w1,w2,w3,w4:(w1-w3)*(w2-w4)/((w1-w4)*(w2-w3)); simplify(cr(f(z1),f(z2),f(z3),f(z4))-cr(z1,z2,z3,z4))
checkable.asserts: The cross-ratio is Möbius-invariant. So among n points, only n−3 invariants are essential; the expected result is 0.

checkable.sympy: t=symbols('t'); P=Function('P')(t); Q=Function('Q')(t); K1=Function('K1')(t); K2=Function('K2')(t); W=K1*K2.diff(t)-K2*K1.diff(t); expr=W.diff(t).subs({K1.diff(t,2):-P*K1.diff(t)-Q*K1, K2.diff(t,2):-P*K2.diff(t)-Q*K2}); simplify(expr+P*W)
checkable.asserts: Abel's identity W' = −P W for y'' + P y' + Q y = 0. Hence the Wronskian is Const·exp(−∫P), which is the 'Const·dv/dt' relation on the next page; the expected result is 0.
The derivative of H = K2/K1 equals W/K1^2. A common multiplicative constant on K1 and K2 cancels in H; the expected result is 0.

checkable.sympy: t,a,b,c,d=symbols('t a b c d'); h=Function('h')(t); S=lambda f:diff(f,t,3)/diff(f,t)-Rational(3,2)*(diff(f,t,2)/diff(f,t))**2; simplify(S((a*h+b)/(c*h+d))-S(h))
checkable.asserts: The Schwarzian derivative is invariant under η -> (αη+β)/(γη+δ). So the ratio of solutions is determined only up to a Möbius map: 3 complex = 6 real constants. The expected result is 0.

transcription_corrections: The page is a letter or referee report by a later mathematician (probably H. A. Schwarz) about Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's minimal-surface paper. It is not a Riemann autograph. The archival attribution 'Riemann manuscript' should be noted as misleading.
In 'von den [-2A-] +B+C+E Constanten', the struck symbol is illegible in the image. Only '+B+C+E' and the later '2A+B+C+E' are clear.
The list of quantities appears as 'a, a', b, c, e'. It carries an extra struck or overwritten symbol after a, a'.

The struck sentence beginning '[-Ob meinerseits eine Berichtigung besteht…' is very uncertain. Only the fragments 'multiplicative Constante, die bei u vorkommt, als eine wesentliche Constante mitzuzählen, will ich dahin gestellt sein lassen' are reasonably legible.
In the crossed-out bracket, the constants of formula 16 read 'α, α', ϑ(?)' rather than securely 'β'.
'C. Haller' on the next page is uncertain.
